title: setQueryData
subtitle: Manually set query data
description: Manually set or update the cached data for a query. Supports both direct values and updater functions for accessing previous data. Useful for optimistic updates, cache invalidation, and programmatic data management.

rows.name: queryKey
rows.description: Unique identifier for the query. Can be a string or array of strings/numbers.

rows.name: dataOrUpdater
rows.description: New data to set directly, or an updater function that receives the previous data and returns the new data.

examples.title: Direct Update
examples.description: Set query data directly with a value

examples.title: Functional Update
examples.description: Use an updater function to access previous data

examples.title: Optimistic Updates
examples.description: Update data optimistically before server response

examples.title: Array Operations
examples.description: Add, remove, or update items in array data

examples.title: Cache Invalidation

behavior.title: Immediate Update
behavior.description: Updates cache immediately and triggers re-renders

behavior.title: Functional Updates
behavior.description: Pass a function to access previous data: (prev) => newData

behavior.title: Optimistic Updates
behavior.description: Perfect for optimistic UI updates before server confirmation

behavior.title: Equality Check
behavior.description: Skips update if new data equals previous (configurable via equalityStrategy)

dos: Use functional updates when you need access to previous data
Use for optimistic updates in user interactions
Handle null/undefined in updater functions: (prev ?? defaultValue)
Handle error cases by reverting optimistic updates
Use for cache invalidation and cleanup
donts: Don't use for initial data loading (use fetchQuery instead)
Don't forget to handle error cases in optimistic updates
Don't mutate the previous data object directly in updater
Don't use without understanding the impact on components

callouts.title: Functional Updates
callouts.content: Use the updater function pattern when you need to base the new state on the previous value. This is safer than reading and then writing, as it avoids race conditions.

callouts.title: Handle Undefined
callouts.content: The previous value in updater functions can be undefined. Always handle this case: (prev) => (prev ?? defaultValue) + 1
